name: Serine Biosynthesis Pathway Deficiency, Infantile/Juvenile Form

criteria.description: Low plasma and cerebrospinal fluid serine concentrations
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding serine biosynthesis enzymes (e.g., PHGDH, PSAT1, PSPH)
Presence of developmental delay, microcephaly, and seizures in infancy or early childhood
Clinical and biochemical improvement upon L-serine supplementation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low serine levels plus pathogenic variants in serine biosynthesis genes and compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by biochemical assays and confirmed by molecular genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Often present at birth or early infancy
Seizures resistant to conventional antiepileptic drugs
searchTerms: seizures starting in infancy that are hard to control

pathognomonic.notes: Marked delay in motor and cognitive milestones
searchTerms: very delayed movement and thinking skills
severe delay in learning and motor skills

common.notes: Poor sucking and swallowing in infancy
Increased muscle tone developing over time

searchTerms: poor nerve insulation on brain scan

laboratory: Low plasma and cerebrospinal fluid L-serine concentrations
Elevated 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase enzyme activity in fibroblasts (if tested)
imaging: MRI showing delayed myelination and cerebral atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in PHGDH, PSAT1, or PSPH genes
other: Clinical improvement with oral L-serine supplementation
Electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities consistent with epileptic encephalopathy

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated glycine levels in plasma and CSF
Distinct EEG pattern with burst suppression
Seizures responsive to pyridoxine (vitamin B6) supplementation

redFlags: Early-onset intractable seizures unresponsive to standard antiepileptic drugs
Congenital microcephaly with severe developmental delay
Low serine levels in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid
references: de Koning TJ. Serine biosynthesis disorders. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(4):609-619.
Hart C, et al. Clinical and biochemical features of serine biosynthesis defects. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020;15(1):123.
Orphanet: Serine biosynthesis pathway deficiency, infantile/juvenile form. ORPHA:583595.
